title: The Cosmos
description: Deep space, planets and the Sun from Hubble, Webb, Chandra and NASA's planetary missions.

items.title: Pillars of Creation
items.description_narrative: Towering columns of dust rise in gold and copper tones against a deep blue field, resembling spires and arches carved from a desert landscape. Captured in near-infrared light by the James Webb Space Telescope, these pillars are filled with semi-transparent gas and dust and mark a region where young stars are still forming.
items.tags: nebula, pillars of creation, webb telescope, star formation, infrared, eagle nebula, gas and dust
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI), Anton Koekemoer (STScI), Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Cosmic Cliffs Carina Nebula
items.description_narrative: Webb's near-infrared camera reveals the edge of the star-forming region NGC 3324, nicknamed the Cosmic Cliffs, roughly 7,600 light-years away in the Carina Nebula. Jagged, amber ridges of gas and dust rise like a mountain range across the frame, with countless spiked stars scattered against the deep blue sky above.
items.tags: nebula, carina nebula, webb telescope, star formation, cosmic cliffs, space
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI

items.title: Hubble Ultra Deep Field
items.description_narrative: Countless tiny galaxies of every shape and color speckle a black field, from faint smudges to bright spiral disks. Known as the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, this view of nearly 10,000 galaxies is the deepest visible-light image of the cosmos, a core sample cutting across billions of light-years.
items.tags: galaxies, deep field, hubble, deep space, astrophotography, cosmology
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, S. Beckwith (STScI) and the HUDF Team

items.title: Sombrero Galaxy
items.description_narrative: The galaxy appears almost edge-on, a bright white bulge wrapped in a thin band of dust that blocks light from stars behind it. Captured with Webb's NIRCam camera, it lies around 30 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo, its core holding roughly 2,000 globular clusters of old stars.
items.tags: galaxy, spiral galaxy, edge-on galaxy, dust lane, infrared image, webb, globular clusters, virgo
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI

items.title: Crab Nebula
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: In this Webb infrared view, the Crab Nebula appears as a cage-like lattice of orange-red filaments wrapped around a pale blue-white interior. That soft white haze is synchrotron radiation, thrown off by particles spiraling near light-speed around a neutron star's magnetic field. The nebula lies roughly 6,500 light-years away in the constellation Taurus.
items.tags: crab nebula, supernova remnant, nebula, webb, infrared, synchrotron radiation
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Tea Temim (Princeton University); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Horsehead Nebula
items.description_narrative: A brilliant, diffraction-spiked star blazes above the reddish sky, while the pale blue-white crest of the Horsehead Nebula rises from the bottom of the frame like a cloud-wrapped mane, its edges laced with wispy hydrogen gas. Small distant galaxies dot the dark background around the glowing star. This portion of the nebula's mane is about 0.8 light-years wide.
items.tags: horsehead nebula, webb, nebula, star formation, infrared, hydrogen gas
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, Karl Misselt (University of Arizona), Alain Abergel (IAS, CNRS)

items.title: Andromeda Galaxy
items.description_narrative: A vast spiral galaxy stretches nearly edge-on, its golden core fading into blue-tinged dust lanes and scattered stars. This mosaic, assembled from more than 600 overlapping Hubble exposures taken over a decade, is the largest such portrait ever made of the Andromeda galaxy, which lies 2.5 million light-years away.
items.tags: galaxy, spiral galaxy, andromeda, hubble, mosaic, astrophotography, deep space
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, Benjamin F. Williams (UWashington), Zhuo Chen (UWashington), L. Clifton Johnson (Northwestern); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Veil Nebula
items.description_narrative: Delicate, ribbon-like filaments of red, gold, blue, and purple light drift diagonally across a dark, star-flecked sky, tangled together like threads of torn cloth. These are the remains of the Veil Nebula, debris from a star that exploded about 8,000 years ago, now spanning 110 light-years and lying roughly 2,100 light-years away in Cygnus.
items.tags: supernova remnant, veil nebula, hubble, cygnus constellation, nebula filaments, gas cloud, nebula
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, Hubble Heritage Project

items.title: Southern Ring Nebula Webb
items.description_narrative: Two side-by-side views show the same ring around a central star, the left panel soft and cloud-like, the right revealing intricate shells and radiating spikes of dust. Captured by the James Webb Space Telescope combining near- and mid-infrared light, the left image highlights hot gas recently ejected from the central star of the nebula.
items.tags: nebula, southern ring nebula, webb telescope, planetary nebula, infrared, composite image, space
items.credit_line: The Webb Space Telescope Studies the Southern Ring Nebula

items.title: Stephan's Quintet Webb
items.description_narrative: Five galaxies cluster together against a dense starfield, their spiral arms and glowing cores overlapping in a tangle of blue haze and golden dust. This mosaic, the largest Webb Space Telescope image at the time, combines nearly 1,000 exposures from its near- and mid-infrared instruments to capture the group known as Stephan's Quintet.
items.tags: galaxies, stephans quintet, webb telescope, galaxy cluster, mosaic, infrared, space
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI

items.title: Eagle Nebula
items.description_narrative: A towering pillar of dust rises against a hazy blue backdrop, its ragged silhouette rimmed with orange light from unseen stars beyond. Part of the Eagle Nebula, this pillar spans about ten light-years and marks a stellar nursery of forming stars; the image was released for the Hubble telescope's fifteenth anniversary.
items.tags: nebula, eagle nebula, pillar, star formation, hubble, dust, space
items.credit_line: The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA), ESA, NASA

items.title: Tarantula Nebula Webb
items.description_narrative: Rust-red clouds of dust swirl around a bright, densely packed cluster of blue-white stars at the center of the frame. This image from the James Webb Space Telescope's Near-Infrared Camera stretches 340 light-years across and reveals tens of thousands of young stars once hidden by cosmic dust, with the most active region sparkling pale blue.
items.tags: nebula, tarantula nebula, webb telescope, star formation, infrared, gas and dust, space
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Webb ERO Production Team

items.title: Helix Nebula
items.description_narrative: A luminous red core sits inside a swirling teal ring flecked with fine filaments, giving the whole scene the look of a giant cosmic eye. Captured in infrared by NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope, this nebula lies about 700 light-years away in the constellation Aquarius and marks the death of a sun-like star.
items.tags: nebula, helix nebula, planetary nebula, spitzer, infrared, aquarius, dying star
items.credit_line: NASA - Comets Kick up Dust in Helix Nebula

items.title: Ring Nebula
items.description_narrative: A glowing ring of blue-green gas encircles a hazy interior, surrounded by faint red filaments radiating outward like petals. This composite combines visible light from the Hubble Space Telescope with infrared data from the Large Binocular Telescope, revealing a football-shaped structure filling the interior of the nebula rather than leaving it empty.
items.tags: nebula, ring nebula, planetary nebula, hubble, composite image, gas, space
items.credit_line: HubbleSite Release Image: STScI-2013-13 - NASA's Hubble Space Telescope Reveals the Ring Nebula's True Shape

items.title: Orion Nebula
items.description_narrative: Billowing clouds of pink, orange, and violet gas surround a bright central cavity ringed with dust and scattered stars. This mosaic reveals the star-forming heart of the Orion Nebula in unprecedented detail, home to more than 3,000 stars of various sizes and shaped by the ultraviolet radiation of four massive young stars at its center.
items.tags: nebula, orion nebula, star formation, hubble, trapezium, gas and dust, astrophotography
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, Hubble Space Telescope Orion Treasury Project Team, Massimo Robberto (STScI, ESA)

items.title: Pinwheel Galaxy
items.description_narrative: M101, the Pinwheel Galaxy, sits about 21 million light-years away in this composite that combines purple X-ray data from Chandra with visible light from Hubble. Spiral arms of purple and violet wind clockwise around a bright golden-white core, dotted with scattered points of light.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, x-ray, chandra, hubble, composite image, pinwheel galaxy
items.credit_line: X-ray: NASA/CXC/Univ. of Alabama/M. Muhibullah et al.; Optical: NASA/ESA/STScI; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/N. Wolk

items.title: Antennae Galaxies
items.description_narrative: Two spiral galaxies collide in a slow-motion firestorm, their star-studded arms tangled into a curved streamer laced with dark dust lanes and pink knots of new stars. Cataloged as NGC 4038 and NGC 4039, the two galaxies began colliding a few hundred million years ago, igniting new star formation as they merge.
items.tags: galaxy collision, spiral galaxy, interacting galaxies, star formation, hubble, astrophotography, deep space
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration; Acknowledgment: B. Whitmore (STScI)

items.title: Mystic Mountain
items.description_narrative: A craggy peak of gas and dust rises from a hazy cloudscape streaked with wisps and dotted with bright stars. Part of the Carina Nebula, 7,500 light-years away, this three-light-year-tall pillar is being eroded by light from nearby stars, its infant stars shooting jets of gas from its peaks.
items.tags: nebula, carina nebula, star formation, pillar, hubble, gas and dust, space
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, Hubble 20th Anniversary Team, Mario Livio (STScI)

items.title: Butterfly Nebula NGC 6302
items.description_narrative: Two glowing lobes of gas billow outward from a bright central waist, edged in orange and threaded with fine filaments against a starry background. This planetary nebula, NGC 6302, is the expanding wreckage of a dying sun-like star, its wings spanning more than two light-years as gas rushes outward at over 600,000 miles an hour.
items.tags: nebula, planetary nebula, butterfly nebula, ngc 6302, hubble, dying star, gas
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble SM4 ERO Team

items.title: Cartwheel Galaxy Webb
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: Webb's composite view shows the Cartwheel Galaxy, formed by a high-speed collision about 400 million years ago, alongside its two smaller companion galaxies. A bright inner ring and a wider outer ring are linked by glowing red spokes, with blue dust and scattered background galaxies filling the surrounding field.
items.tags: galaxy, cartwheel galaxy, webb telescope, galaxy collision, infrared, space
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Webb ERO Production Team

items.title: Cosmic Reef
items.description_narrative: Nicknamed the Cosmic Reef, this Hubble portrait shows the giant red nebula NGC 2014 beside its smaller blue neighbor NGC 2020, both 163,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud. A cluster of bright stars glows amid coral-like orange bubbles, while a separate ring of blue gas glows apart at lower left.
items.tags: nebula, hubble, star cluster, large magellanic cloud, emission nebula, space
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA and STScI

items.title: Jupiter's Great Red Spot
items.description_narrative: Swirling bands of cream, tan, and blue-gray clouds churn across this close view of Jupiter's turbulent atmosphere, dominated by the oval form of the Great Red Spot. Delicate white filaments and turbulent eddies trace the surrounding atmosphere. Voyager 1 captured the scene through color filters that were later recombined into this single image.
items.tags: jupiter, great red spot, voyager 1, planetary atmosphere, gas giant, space photography
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL

items.title: Pluto New Horizons
items.description_narrative: A cratered, tan-and-brown world fills the frame, one hemisphere marked by a broad pale heart-shaped region set against darker terrain. Captured by NASA's New Horizons spacecraft on July 14, 2015, this natural-color image shows the icy, nitrogen-and-methane-rich plain called Sputnik Planitia at the center of the bright heart.
items.tags: pluto, new horizons, dwarf planet, sputnik planitia, nasa, planetary science, space
items.credit_line: 10 Years Ago: NASA’s New Horizons Captures Pluto’s Heart

items.title: Curiosity Self-Portrait at Mars
items.description_narrative: A six-wheeled rover sits on cracked, sun-baked rock beneath a dusty pink sky, its robotic arm folded beside a drilled patch of stone. This self-portrait of NASA's Curiosity rover, taken at the Mojave site on Mount Sharp, combines dozens of images from the Mars Hand Lens Imager camera on its arm, taken in January 2015.
items.tags: mars, rover, curiosity, self-portrait, nasa, mount sharp, space exploration
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS

items.title: Saturn from Cassini
items.description_narrative: A pale gold planet tilts beneath broad, banded rings that sweep from edge to edge, with a faint blue arc visible where the far rings catch the light. Composited from Cassini spacecraft images taken on February 9, 2004, from 69.4 million kilometers away, the smallest features visible here span about 540 kilometers.
items.tags: saturn, cassini, rings, planet, nasa, solar system, space
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute

items.title: Centaurus A Crop
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: Webb's infrared view of Centaurus A exposes a warped disk of gas and dust left by a collision with another galaxy billions of years ago; the grainy glow is actually millions of resolved stars. A diagonal band of fiery orange dust cuts across a hazy blue-white glow, framed by scattered stars on a dark background.
items.tags: galaxy, centaurus a, webb telescope, infrared, galaxy collision, space
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI), Joseph DePasquale (STScI), Macarena Garcia Marin (ESA Office at STScI)

items.title: Cat’s Paw Nebula
items.description_narrative: Webb's near-infrared view scratches beneath the surface of the Cat's Paw Nebula, a massive star-forming region about 4,000 light-years away in the constellation Scorpius, where massive young stars carve cavities into the surrounding gas and dust. Glowing blue cavities open within thick rust-colored clouds, dense with pinpoint stars throughout the frame.
items.tags: nebula, cat's paw nebula, webb telescope, star formation, infrared, space
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI

items.title: The Carina Nebula: Star Birth in the Extreme
items.description_narrative: A 50-light-year-wide panorama of the central Carina Nebula, 7,500 light-years away, where intense radiation from massive stars is sculpting the surrounding gas even as it triggers new star birth. Billowing clouds in gold, rust, and pale blue-white sweep across the frame, pierced by dark dust clumps and small knots of bright stars.
items.tags: nebula, carina nebula, hubble, star formation, emission nebula, space
items.credit_line: Hubble Image: NASA, ESA, N. Smith (University of California, Berkeley), and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA); CTIO Image: N. Smith (University of California, Berkeley) and NOAO/AURA/NSF

items.title: Rho Ophiuchi
items.description_narrative: The Rho Ophiuchi cloud complex, the closest star-forming region to Earth, glows with jets of hydrogen thrown off by young stars in this Webb image. Red streaks of ejected gas cross a dark upper field, while a pale golden cave of dust opens below, ringed by sharp, bright stars.
items.tags: star formation, nebula, webb telescope, infrared, young stars, molecular cloud
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Klaus Pontoppidan (STScI); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Hubble Photographs Grand Design Spiral Galaxy M81
items.description_narrative: Hubble's sharp, tilted view shows a golden spiral galaxy with a brilliant core and smooth arms flecked with blue clusters of young, hot stars. Fine dust lanes wind inward toward the glowing nucleus, and scattered stars fill the surrounding dark field. This is M81, a spiral galaxy about 11.6 million light-years away and roughly the apparent size of the full Moon in our sky.
items.tags: m81, spiral galaxy, hubble, star clusters, galaxy, bode's galaxy
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

items.title: NGC 346
items.description_narrative: Pink clouds of hot, ionized hydrogen thread through orange ridges of colder, dust-laden gas in this Webb view of NGC 346, a star cluster embedded in a nebula within the Small Magellanic Cloud, 200,000 light-years away. Light from young stars is eroding the dense clouds, carving the pillars and ridges seen throughout.
items.tags: ngc 346, small magellanic cloud, star cluster, webb telescope, infrared imaging, nebula
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, CSA, Olivia Jones (UK ATC), Guido De Marchi (ESTEC), Margaret Meixner (USRA); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI), Nolan Habel (USRA), Laura Lenkić (USRA), Laurie Chu (NASA Ames)

items.title: Out of This Whirl: the Whirlpool Galaxy (M51) and Companion Galaxy
items.description_narrative: The Whirlpool Galaxy (M51), a face-on spiral about 31 million light-years away, appears beside its smaller companion galaxy NGC 5195, which Hubble shows passing behind rather than merging with it. Two sweeping blue-white arms laced with dark dust lanes and pink star-forming knots spiral around a bright yellow core.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, whirlpool galaxy, companion galaxy, hubble, star formation, dust lanes
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, S. Beckwith (STScI), and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

items.title: Webb’s First Deep Field Unveiled
items.description_narrative: Countless small galaxies in white and orange dot a black sky, some smeared into thin curving arcs, beside a brilliant star with long blue diffraction spikes. This is the galaxy cluster SMACS 0723, shown as it appeared 4.6 billion years ago; its mass bends light like a lens, stretching background galaxies into the arcs seen here.
items.tags: deep field, galaxy cluster, webb, smacs 0723, gravitational lensing, infrared image, distant galaxies
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI

items.title: Herbig-Haro 46/47
items.description_narrative: Webb's huge diffraction spikes mark a buried, tightly bound pair of young stars, glowing as an orange-white core amid two opposing orange lobes of earlier gas ejections. A faint blue haze of nebula material wraps around the lobes, threaded by thin blue lines from the stars' more recent outflows. This is Herbig-Haro 46/47, a region about 3.1 light-years across.
items.tags: herbig-haro object, protostar, webb, nebula, star formation, outflow
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI), Anton Koekemoer (STScI)

items.title: Bubble Nebula (NGC 7635)
items.description_narrative: A massive, super-hot star blows this bubble of gas into space; the Bubble Nebula is 7 light-years across and lies 7,100 light-years away in the constellation Cassiopeia. The star sits off-center near the bubble's edge, its blue shell rimmed by dense golden-orange pillars of gas and dust, with scattered stars piercing the surrounding dark.
items.tags: nebula, bubble nebula, hubble, star, emission nebula, space
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

items.title: L1527 and Protostar
items.description_narrative: An hourglass of glowing gas surrounds a hidden protostar in this Webb image of the dark cloud L1527. The upper lobe blazes orange and red with wispy filaments, while the lower lobe glows blue, since less dust lies between it and the telescope. A dusty band pinches across the center, hiding the still-forming star.
items.tags: protostar, l1527, molecular cloud, webb telescope, infrared imaging, star formation
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI), Alyssa Pagan (STScI), Anton Koekemoer (STScI)

items.title: M82 Cigar Galaxy — Webb & Hubble Composite
items.description_narrative: Fiery plumes of orange-red dust erupt above and below the blue-white disk of the edge-on starburst galaxy M82, nicknamed the Cigar Galaxy, in this Webb and Hubble composite. Extreme star formation drives the plumes, and yellow filaments of ionized hydrogen glow nearest the disk. Webb resolves about 16.5 million individual stars here.
items.tags: m82, cigar galaxy, starburst galaxy, webb telescope, stellar plumes, infrared imaging
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, Adam Smercina (STScI, Tufts), Thomas Williams (University of Manchester); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: NASA Unveils Celestial Fireworks as Official Hubble 25th Anniversary Image
items.description_narrative: A dense cluster of young stars blazes at the heart of this Hubble view of the nebula Gum 29, ringed by pillars of orange-brown dust and blue-green haze. The cluster, called Westerlund 2, holds about 3,000 stars and lies roughly 20,000 light-years away in Carina. Red marks glowing hydrogen; the greenish-blue hues are oxygen.
items.tags: westerlund 2, gum 29, star cluster, carina, hubble, nebula
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA), A. Nota (ESA/STScI), and the Westerlund 2 Science Team

items.title: Spiral Galaxy M83
items.description_narrative: This face-on spiral galaxy has a bright orange core wrapped in dark dust lanes, with pink patches of glowing gas tracing star formation along its arms. Known as M83, or the Southern Pinwheel, it lies 15 million light-years away in the constellation Hydra and spans about 50,000 light-years, home to thousands of star clusters.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, southern pinwheel, star formation, dust lanes, hubble, hydra constellation, star clusters
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA); Acknowledgement: W. Blair (STScI/Johns Hopkins University) and R. O'Connell (University of Virginia)

items.title: WR 124
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: A brilliant star with long, sharp diffraction spikes sits at the center of a rounded magenta and orange nebula threaded with darker clumpy lanes, set against a dense starfield. This is Wolf-Rayet 124, an aging star whose ejected nebula spans about 10 light-years, its clumps shaped by stellar winds streaming outward.
items.tags: wolf-rayet star, nebula, wr 124, webb, infrared image, stellar wind, dust
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Webb ERO Production Team

items.title: Lagoon Nebula — Visible Light
items.description_narrative: Ridges and cavities of glowing gas fill this visible-light view of the Lagoon Nebula's heart, sculpted by the massive young star Herschel 36 near center. Blue-green oxygen marks where dust has blown away, while red nitrogen and dark purple gas dominate the surrounding clouds. Herschel 36 is about 32 times as massive as the Sun.
items.tags: lagoon nebula, herschel 36, star formation, nebula, visible light, hubble
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and STScI

items.title: Pismis 24
items.description_narrative: Pismis 24, a young star cluster in the Lobster Nebula about 5,500 light-years away, blazes with brilliant stars against a deep blue backdrop in this Webb image. Below, a jagged golden-orange peak of dust rises through wisps of pale cloud toward the cluster's light.
items.tags: star cluster, nebula, webb telescope, infrared, lobster nebula, star formation
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: A “Rose” Made of Galaxies Highlights Hubble’s 21st Anniversary
items.description_narrative: Arp 273, a pair of interacting spiral galaxies about 300 million light-years away, forms a rose-like shape as the larger galaxy's disk is tidally distorted by its smaller companion below. Pale golden spiral arms edged in blue star clusters curl around a bright core, trailing down toward a smaller, warped companion galaxy.
items.tags: interacting galaxies, spiral galaxy, hubble, arp 273, galaxy collision, star clusters
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

items.title: Barred Spiral Galaxy NGC 1300
items.description_narrative: The barred spiral galaxy NGC 1300 lies roughly 69 million light-years away in the constellation Eridanus, with a straight central bar of stars feeding its spiral arms. Blue star clusters and reddish dust lanes trace the winding arms, and faint background galaxies dot the surrounding darkness.
items.tags: barred spiral galaxy, ngc 1300, hubble, galaxy, star clusters, space
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA); Acknowledgment: P. Knezek (WIYN)

items.title: The Greatest Saturn Portrait ...Yet
items.description_narrative: Cassini's sweeping portrait of Saturn combines 126 separate images into one seamless mosaic spanning the planet and its full ring system. Subtle bands of gold and cream color the globe, while the planet's own shadow falls darkly across the rings at left. The spacecraft was roughly 3.9 million miles away when it captured the view over about two hours.
items.tags: saturn, rings, cassini, mosaic, planet, space exploration
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute

items.title: NGC 604
items.description_narrative: A star-forming region in the Triangulum galaxy, 2.73 million light-years away, imaged in infrared light. Stellar winds from young, hot stars carve dark cavities into surrounding gas and dust, ringed by orange filaments and a pale blue-white glow at the core.
items.tags: nebula, star-forming region, infrared, webb telescope, spiral galaxy, stellar winds
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI

items.title: Spiral Galaxy UGC 2885
items.description_narrative: A vast spiral galaxy fills the frame, its pale core wrapped in loose blue arms, with a brilliant foreground star's sharp diffraction spikes beside the nucleus. Nicknamed Rubin's galaxy after astronomer Vera Rubin, UGC 2885 lies 232 million light-years away in Perseus, 2.5 times wider than the Milky Way with 10 times as many stars.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, ugc 2885, hubble, perseus constellation, diffraction spikes, large galaxy, rubin's galaxy
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, Benne Holwerda (University of Louisville)

items.title: NGC 1333
items.description_narrative: A brilliant blue-white star blazes at the top of this Hubble view of NGC 1333, a star-forming region about 960 light-years away, its light scattering through veils of fine dust. Dark dust obscures much of the frame, thickest toward the bottom, where reddish jets of ionized hydrogen mark newly forming stars.
items.tags: ngc 1333, star formation, perseus molecular cloud, hubble, stellar jets, nebula
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, STScI; Image Processing: Varun Bajaj (STScI), Joseph DePasquale (STScI), Jennifer Mack (STScI)

items.title: Pandora’s Cluster
items.description_narrative: Webb's infrared view of Pandora's Cluster captures an estimated 50,000 sources of light, where several massive galaxy clusters are merging into one megacluster. Its enormous mass bends space so strongly that distant background galaxies appear as faint red streaks and arcs among the white glowing cluster members.
items.tags: galaxy cluster, gravitational lensing, webb telescope, infrared, deep field, megacluster
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, CSA, Ivo Labbe (Swinburne), Rachel Bezanson (University of Pittsburgh); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Galaxies IC 2163 and NGC 2207
items.description_narrative: Two overlapping spiral galaxies fill the frame, cataloged as IC 2163 at left and the larger NGC 2207 at right. Clusters of young blue stars fleck their red, dust-laced spiral arms, which wind around two brilliant cores. The pair grazed one another millions of years ago and together form the equivalent of two dozen Sun-sized stars a year, far more than the Milky Way's two or three, lying about 114 million light-years from Earth.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, ic 2163, ngc 2207, interacting galaxies, star formation, webb
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI

items.title: A Farewell to Saturn
items.description_narrative: Cassini's last portrait of Saturn shows the planet as a dark crescent rimmed with warm gold light, cradled inside its broad, glowing rings. The spacecraft was about 698,000 miles from Saturn when it captured this final mosaic, two days before diving into the planet's atmosphere and ending its mission.
items.tags: saturn, rings, cassini, planet, final image, space exploration
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute

items.title: Actively Forming Star System Lynds 483
items.description_narrative: Webb's near-infrared camera captures Lynds 483, the shimmering ejections of two actively forming stars 650 light-years away in the constellation Serpens. Twin lobes of orange and magenta gas flare upward and downward from a bright central point, threaded with fine dark filaments against a dense field of stars.
items.tags: nebula, protostar, webb telescope, infrared, bipolar outflow, space
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI

items.title: The Cone Nebula (NGC 2264)
items.description_narrative: Located about 2,500 light-years away, the Cone Nebula (NGC 2264) is a towering pillar of gas and dust silhouetted against a glowing red nebula. Its dark, textured column rises to a bright, blue-white crown of light, with scattered pinpoint stars set against the surrounding crimson glow.

items.title: Image of Sun From NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory
items.description_narrative: The Sun glows gold, its turbulent surface mottled with dark filaments and looping bright flares near the edges. Darker patches trace cooler regions across the disk, and a faint halo of light extends beyond it into space.

items.credit_line: NASA/GSFC/Solar Dynamics Observatory

items.title: NGC 6072
items.description_narrative: NASA's Webb telescope shows planetary nebula NGC 6072 as multiple outflows from a dying central star push gas outward at different angles, forming a disk. Glowing red molecular gas surrounds a bright white core, spreading into billowing orange clouds across the frame.
items.tags: planetary nebula, webb telescope, infrared, dying star, molecular gas, outflow
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI

items.title: The Omega Nebula (Swan Nebula/M17)
items.description_narrative: The Omega Nebula (M17), a star-forming cloud in the Milky Way about 5,500 light-years away, was imaged in visible light by Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. Swirling green, pink and gold clouds of glowing gas and dust wrap around newly formed stars, cut through by dark dust lanes.
items.tags: nebula, star formation, hubble, milky way, gas and dust, emission nebula

items.title: “The Mice” (NGC 4676): Colliding Galaxies Stream Stars and Gas
items.description_narrative: A long blue tail of stars and gas streams from one core toward the upper right in this Hubble view of "The Mice," a pair of colliding galaxies cataloged as NGC 4676. Dust lanes lace the two glowing cores as they merge. The pair lies about 300 million light-years away.
