items.title: 30 Doradus B
items.description_narrative: An X-ray, optical, and infrared composite of the supernova remnant 30 Doradus B, 160,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud, where astronomers found evidence of at least two exploded stars. Purple X-ray light traces a faint shell through pink, blue, and red clouds, with bright stars scattered across the frame.
items.tags: supernova remnant, x-ray, nebula, composite image, large magellanic cloud, star formation
items.credit_line: X-ray: NASA/CXC/Penn State Univ./L. Townsley et al.; Optical: NASA/STScI/HST; Infrared: NASA/JPL/CalTech/SST; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/J. Schmidt, N. Wolk, K. Arcand

items.title: FS Tau
items.description_narrative: Webb's diffraction-spiked glare marks the young star system FS Tau, wrapped in swirling orange and red outflows of gas and soot-like dust, with pale blue nebulosity drifting to the right where starlight scatters off fine grains. Countless faint background galaxies, tinted by how much dust lies in front of them, dot the dark surrounding field. The portion imaged is about 0.31 light-years across.
items.tags: fs tau, protostar, webb, nebula, star formation, young star
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Trifid Nebula
items.description_narrative: A tall, dark brown pillar of dust rises against a blue haze at upper left, its edge glowing gold, with bright orange stars scattered through the surrounding clouds. This is the Trifid Nebula, a star-forming region about 5,000 light-years away, where color marks density: blue where dust is thinnest and near-black in the densest pockets.
items.tags: nebula, trifid nebula, star-forming region, hubble, dust pillars, emission nebula, young stars
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Planetary Nebula NGC 2899
items.description_narrative: Planetary nebula NGC 2899 glows from hydrogen and oxygen lit by a white dwarf at its center, roughly 4,500 light-years away in the constellation Vela. A blue-green cavity opens at the middle of the nebula, rimmed by billowing orange and rust-colored clouds and dotted with sharp points of starlight.
items.tags: planetary nebula, hubble, white dwarf, glowing gas, nebula, vela constellation
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Herbig-Haro 49/50
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: A tall plume of reddish-orange gas surges diagonally across the frame, its wake-like arcs carved by a jet from a still-forming star just off the lower right edge. Near the top, a small blue-tinted spiral glimmers by chance alignment far beyond the outflow. This portion of Herbig-Haro 49/50 spans about 0.3 light-years.
items.tags: herbig-haro object, outflow, webb, nebula, protostar, spiral galaxy
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI

items.title: A Splendor Seldom Seen
items.description_narrative: Saturn appears as a dark, greenish silhouette ringed by a luminous halo of gold and tan bands, backlit so its rings blaze with reflected light. Captured by NASA's Cassini spacecraft in Saturn's shadow, the image also shows two of Saturn's moons, Enceladus and Tethys, as faint points near the rings.
items.tags: saturn, planetary rings, cassini, backlit, moons, enceladus, tethys, solar system
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute

items.title: Dwarf Galaxy WLM
items.description_narrative: Webb resolves the dwarf galaxy WLM into a scatter of faint individual stars, seen here as countless reddish and white points across a starry field, with a bright, cross-spiked star and several distant background spiral galaxies also in view. The portion imaged spans about 1,700 light-years.
items.tags: dwarf galaxy, wlm, webb, stars, infrared, galaxies
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, CSA, Kristen McQuinn (Rutgers University); Image Processing: Zoltan Levay (STScI)

items.title: Little Dumbbell Nebula
items.description_narrative: Two translucent lobes of gas, joined at a bright white waist, form this Hubble portrait of the Little Dumbbell Nebula, also known as Messier 76, located 3,400 light-years away in Perseus. The lobes are inflating away from a dying star at the center; red marks glowing nitrogen and blue marks oxygen.
items.tags: little dumbbell nebula, messier 76, planetary nebula, perseus, hubble, dying star
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, STScI

items.title: Starry Splendor in Core of Omega Centauri
items.description_narrative: Thousands of stars in gold, white, and pale blue pack tightly together, thinning toward the edges of the frame into darkness. This is the core of Omega Centauri, a globular cluster of about 10 million stars lying roughly 17,000 light-years away, among the largest of some 200 such clusters orbiting the Milky Way.
items.tags: globular cluster, omega centauri, star cluster, hubble, milky way, dense stars, black hole
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA); Acknowledgment: A. Cool (San Francisco State University) and J. Anderson (STScI)

items.title: Witch Head Brews Baby Stars
items.description_narrative: Wisps of green cloud curve and taper into a shape reminiscent of a hooked profile, scattered with small blue-white stars against a dark sky. This is the Witch Head nebula, a cloud of dust and gas lit up by nearby massive stars, located hundreds of light-years away near the Orion constellation.
items.tags: nebula, witch head nebula, reflection nebula, infrared image, wise, orion constellation, dust cloud
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech

items.title: Spiral Galaxy Pair NGC 4302 and NGC 4298
items.description_narrative: A slender edge-on galaxy glows gold along a dark dust lane at left, while a tilted blue spiral with a bright core sits at right. These are NGC 4302, seen exactly edge-on, and NGC 4298, tilted about 70 degrees, a pair of similar spiral galaxies both roughly 55 million light-years away.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, galaxy pair, edge-on galaxy, dust lane, hubble, virgo cluster, coma berenices
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and M. Mutchler (STScI)

items.title: Cygnus Loop Nebula
items.description_narrative: Ultraviolet light picks out wispy, thread-like filaments of hot gas and dust in the Cygnus Loop, glowing pale blue against a star-flecked black sky. These tendrils are the shockwave from a massive stellar explosion, still spreading outward roughly 1,500 light-years away. The original blast would once have been bright enough to see with the naked eye from Earth.
items.tags: cygnus loop, nebula, supernova remnant, ultraviolet, galex, filaments
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech

items.title: The Rite of Spring
items.description_narrative: This Cassini mosaic, built from 75 exposures, captures Saturn during its equinox, an alignment that occurs only once every 15 Earth years. Low sunlight has dimmed the rings to a narrow, pale arc on one side, fading to darkness on the other, while the planet's cloud bands glow faintly gold above a deep black shadow.
items.tags: saturn, rings, cassini, equinox, natural color, gas giant
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute

items.title: NASA’s Great Observatories Examine the Galactic Center Region
items.description_narrative: Threads of red dust and violet-blue haze swirl around the turbulent core of the Milky Way in this composite of Hubble, Spitzer, and Chandra data. Yellow marks Hubble's infrared view of stellar nurseries; red is Spitzer's infrared dust; blue and violet are Chandra's X-rays from gas heated to millions of degrees. The view spans about 246 light-years.
items.tags: milky way, galactic center, hubble, spitzer, chandra, composite image
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, SSC, CXC, and STScI

items.title: Sagittarius B2
items.description_narrative: Sagittarius B2, a giant molecular cloud near the center of the Milky Way, glows with stars, gas and cosmic dust in this near-infrared Webb image. A dense field of white and blue stars spreads across the frame, framed by soft orange clouds of glowing dust in the upper corners.
items.tags: molecular cloud, milky way, webb telescope, infrared, star field, galactic center
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Adam Ginsburg (University of Florida), Nazar Budaiev (University of Florida), Taehwa Yoo (University of Florida); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Cosmic Ice Sculptures: Dust Pillars in the Carina Nebula
items.description_narrative: In the Carina Nebula, roughly 7,500 light-years away, violent stellar winds and radiation from massive stars carve pillars of cold hydrogen and dust into strange, sculpted shapes. Dark, wispy pillars stand out against a pale blue-white haze streaked with gold, dotted with small bright stars.
items.tags: nebula, carina nebula, hubble, dust pillars, star formation, space
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Project (STScI/AURA); Acknowledgment: M. Livio (STScI) and N. Smith (University of California, Berkeley)

items.title: The Case of the Disappearing Continent
items.description_narrative: In visible light this region resembles North America, but Spitzer's infrared view makes the continent shape disappear, since infrared light passes through dust that blocks visible light. Glowing red clouds fill most of the frame, dotted with countless stars, with darker patches of thick dust and a wedge of blue-black sky in the upper corner.
items.tags: nebula, north america nebula, spitzer, infrared, star field, space
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech

items.title: Star-Forming Region S106
items.description_narrative: Two glowing blue-white lobes spread outward like wings from a bright core wrapped in dark red dust, giving the nebula an hourglass shape scattered with pinpoint stars. Known as Sharpless 2-106, this bipolar star-forming region lies nearly 2,000 light-years away, powered by a massive young star that carves the glowing lobes from gas and dust.
items.tags: nebula, star-forming region, bipolar nebula, hubble, sharpless 2-106, emission nebula, young star
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

items.title: 47 Tucanae – Hubble
items.description_narrative: A Hubble image of the globular cluster 47 Tucanae, a dense swarm of up to a million stars some 16,700 light-years away in the southern constellation Tucana. Countless white and pale blue points crowd the frame, with a scattering of brighter orange stars standing out among them.
items.tags: globular cluster, star cluster, hubble, milky way, space, stars
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, H. Richer and J. Heyl (University of British Columbia), and J. Anderson and J. Kalirai (STScI)

items.title: Global Color Mosaic of Triton
items.description_narrative: A Voyager spacecraft's color mosaic of Triton reveals a mottled globe: cratered tan terrain above, a pale blue-green band of fresh frost circling the equator, and faint pink-tinged terrain toward the bottom associated with a south polar ice cap. Dark streaky markings mark dust deposited by the geyser-like plumes Voyager found still active during its flyby. Triton's surface is the coldest known in the solar system, at 38 K.
items.tags: triton, neptune moon, voyager 2, ice, nitrogen frost, cryovolcanism
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL/USGS

items.title: IC 63 Ghost Nebula
items.description_narrative: Pale gas and dust rise against a dense field of stars, tinted red and blue. This is IC 63, the Ghost Nebula, 550 light-years away in Cassiopeia. Ultraviolet radiation from the blue-giant star Gamma Cassiopeiae makes the hydrogen glow red, while starlight reflects blue off the dust.
items.tags: nebula, ghost nebula, cassiopeia, gas and dust, hubble, space photography
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and STScI Acknowledgment: H. Arab (University of Strasbourg)

items.title: Soul Nebula
items.description_narrative: Green nebular light surrounds a bright orange pillar of dust rising from the center, dotted with sharp blue-white stars. Known as the Soul Nebula (IC 1848 or W5), it is over 150 light-years across and lies about 6,500 light-years away in Cassiopeia, where dusty pillars point toward the young star cluster carving its cavity.
items.tags: nebula, star-forming region, emission nebula, dust pillars, infrared image, wise, cassiopeia, open cluster
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA

items.title: NGC 1546
items.description_narrative: Rusty-brown dust lanes wind across the disk of the galaxy NGC 1546 in this Hubble view, backlit by its own glowing yellow core of older stars. Small blue patches mark active star formation, and a faint edge-on spiral galaxy shows in the background at left. NGC 1546 lies in the constellation Dorado.
items.tags: ngc 1546, spiral galaxy, dorado, dust lanes, hubble, star formation
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, STScI, David Thilker (JHU)

items.title: Enceladus: Trailing Hemisphere
items.description_narrative: Cassini's mosaic of Enceladus' trailing hemisphere shows an icy white globe crossed by long, braided ridges and fine crack-like troughs, with cratered, older terrain lightly speckled across the upper left. A soft diagonal line marks where sunlight falls away toward the unlit side. The mosaic combines 16 separate images taken during a close flyby.
items.tags: enceladus, moon, cassini, ice, cratered terrain, saturn system
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute

items.title: Bat Shadow
items.description_narrative: Around the young star HBC 672, 1,400 light-years away, Hubble captured the shadow of its unseen planet-forming disk stretching across a star-forming cloud, nicknamed the Bat Shadow for its wing-like shape. Two dark, wing-shaped bands fan out from a bright pinpoint of starlight, cutting across drifting blue and amber clouds dotted with sharp, spiked stars.
items.tags: nebula, hubble, young star, planet-forming disk, shadow, space
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and STScI

items.title: MACS 0416
items.description_narrative: Galaxies of every hue crowd this Webb and Hubble composite of the cluster MACS0416, whose gravity bends and magnifies light from more distant background galaxies into faint arcs. The bluest galaxies are relatively close and rich in new stars, while the redder ones are more distant or dust-laden. The cluster lies about 4.3 billion light-years away.
items.tags: macs 0416, galaxy cluster, gravitational lensing, webb telescope, hubble, deep field
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Jose Diego (IFCA), Jordan D'Silva (UWA), Anton Koekemoer (STScI), Jake Summers (ASU), Rogier Windhorst (ASU), Haojing Yan (University of Missouri); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Jet in Carina: WFC3 UVIS Full Field
items.description_narrative: A glowing pillar of gas and dust, tipped in yellow-orange light, rises from a sea of teal nebulosity, with scattered stars punctuating the surrounding blue-black sky. This Hubble image captures a stellar jet in the Carina Nebula, composited from separate exposures taken over about a week in five narrow filters.
items.tags: carina nebula, stellar jet, hubble, gas and dust, star formation, wfc3
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble SM4 ERO Team

items.title: A Cosmic Holiday Ornament, Hubble-Style
items.description_narrative: The planetary nebula NGC 5189, formed as a dying Sun-like star expelled its outer layers, lies between 1,800 and 3,000 light-years away and resembles a glass-blown ornament with a glowing ribbon entwined. Bluish, knotty lobes of gas radiate outward, wrapped by a golden band of filaments, against a dark field scattered with stars.
items.tags: planetary nebula, ngc 5189, hubble, bipolar nebula, space, gas
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

items.title: Dark Clouds in Rosette Nebula
items.description_narrative: Hubble captures a small sliver of the Rosette Nebula, where dark lanes of hydrogen gas laced with dust are silhouetted against glowing blue-gray clouds. Radiation from a cluster of massive stars is eroding this material, and near the upper right a buried young star fires jets of plasma into the cold gas, lighting a faint red glow. This portion spans about four light-years, part of a nebula 100 light-years across and 5,200 light-years from Earth.
items.tags: rosette nebula, dark clouds, nebula, hubble, star formation, hydrogen gas
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: NGC 5335
items.description_narrative: A bright bar of golden light slices across the glowing core of NGC 5335 in this face-on Hubble view, funneling gas inward to fuel star formation. Loose, patchy streamers of blue young stars wind around the center instead of well-defined spiral arms. Such bars appear in about 30 percent of observed galaxies, including the Milky Way.
items.tags: ngc 5335, spiral galaxy, galactic bar, star formation, hubble, flocculent galaxy
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, STScI; Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Trumpler 14
items.description_narrative: A tight swarm of brilliant blue-white stars, some with sharp diffraction spikes, blazes against a soft blue haze streaked with rust-brown clouds. This is Trumpler 14, a star cluster in the Carina Nebula about 8,000 light-years away and only 500,000 years old, among the most massive-star-rich groupings in the Milky Way.
items.tags: star cluster, trumpler 14, carina nebula, hubble, massive stars, open cluster, milky way
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and J. Maíz Apellániz (Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia, Spain); Acknowledgment: N. Smith (University of Arizona)

items.title: JWST Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey
items.description_narrative: Countless faint galaxies of many shapes and colors speckle the blackness in this deep field, with a few bright foreground stars showing prominent diffraction spikes. This infrared image was taken for the JADES survey of the GOODS-South field. More than 45,000 galaxies are visible here, including many that existed when the universe was less than 600 million years old.
items.tags: deep field, galaxies, webb telescope, infrared imaging, cosmology, jades survey
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, Brant Robertson (UC Santa Cruz), Ben Johnson (CfA), Sandro Tacchella (Cambridge), Marcia Rieke (University of Arizona), Daniel Eisenstein (CfA); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: IC 348
items.description_narrative: Webb's near-infrared view shows swirling curtains of pink and violet nebular light, dotted with bright stars flaring sharp diffraction spikes. A looping arc of gas curls along the right side of the frame, likely carved by winds from a hidden pair of massive young stars near the center. This is the star cluster IC 348, imaged across a region about 0.6 light-years wide.
items.tags: ic 348, star cluster, brown dwarf, webb, reflection nebula, star formation
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Kevin Luhman (PSU), Catarina Alves de Oliveira (ESA)

items.title: Lagoon Nebula — Infrared Light
items.description_narrative: Thousands of stars crowd this infrared view of the Lagoon Nebula, many more than appear in visible light, since infrared light pierces the dust that otherwise hides them. Dark, dust-choked Bok globules thread through the haze near the bright cluster at center, anchored by Herschel 36, a star some 200,000 times brighter than the Sun.
items.tags: lagoon nebula, herschel 36, infrared imaging, star cluster, bok globules, hubble
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and STScI

items.title: Galaxy Cluster Abell 370
items.description_narrative: Hundreds of galaxies crowd this Hubble field, their light bent and smeared into faint arcs by the gravity of a massed cluster at the center. Two foreground stars blaze with sharp diffraction spikes amid the swarm of small, faint smudges. This is the giant cluster Abell 370, lying about 4 billion light-years away and containing several hundred galaxies of its own.
items.tags: galaxy cluster, abell 370, gravitational lensing, hubble, dark matter, deep field
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, A. Koekemoer (STScI), M. Jauzac (Durham University), C. Steinhardt (Niels Bohr Institute), and the BUFFALO team

items.title: Star Cluster R136
items.description_narrative: A dense knot of bright blue-white stars glows at the center of a vast, cloudy nebula streaked with orange and brown filaments of gas and dust. This is the young star cluster R136 in the Tarantula Nebula, 170,000 light-years away, home to nine stars each more than 100 times the sun's mass.
items.tags: star cluster, tarantula nebula, r136, hubble, large magellanic cloud, massive stars, nebula
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA, and P. Crowther (University of Sheffield)

items.title: Cassiopeia A — Webb NIRCam
items.description_narrative: Webb's NIRCam view of Cassiopeia A resolves tiny knots of gas from the exploded star, forming clumps of bright orange and pink in the inner shell, ringed by a smoke-like outer shell where ejected material rams into surrounding gas. Sharp, spiked stars scatter across the dark field, with dense clumps in the lower right corner.
items.tags: supernova remnant, cassiopeia a, webb telescope, infrared, nebula, space
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Danny Milisavljevic (Purdue University), Ilse De Looze (UGhent), Tea Temim (Princeton University)

items.title: M82 Cigar Galaxy — Webb NIRCam
items.description_narrative: The edge-on disk of the starburst galaxy M82, the Cigar Galaxy, glows blue-white against fiery orange plumes of gas erupting above and below it in this Webb near-infrared view. The snapshot captures a scene that has been evolving for a couple hundred million years. Webb resolves about 16.5 million individual stars within the galaxy.
items.tags: m82, cigar galaxy, webb telescope, nircam, starburst galaxy, infrared imaging
items.credit_line: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, Adam Smercina (STScI, Tufts), Thomas Williams (University of Manchester); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Cassiopeia A — Chandra X-ray Composite
items.description_narrative: This Chandra, NuSTAR, and Hubble composite of the supernova remnant Cassiopeia A maps elements from its exploded star: iron in red, oxygen in purple, and titanium in blue, about 11,000 light years from Earth. The debris forms a roughly spherical tangle of orange, green, and blue filaments, set against a dark field speckled with stars.
items.tags: supernova remnant, cassiopeia a, x-ray, chandra, composite image, space
items.credit_line: Chandra: NASA/CXC/RIKEN/T. Sato et al.; NuSTAR: NASA/NuSTAR; Hubble: NASA/STScI

items.title: WISE Unveils a Treasure Trove of Beauty
items.description_narrative: Swirling teal and green clouds fill the upper frame, opening onto a bright white core, while a warm red and pink nebula glows in the lower right. This is the Rho Ophiuchi cloud complex, one of the nearest star-forming regions to Earth, its bright core an emission nebula and its red glow starlight reflected off dust.
items.tags: nebula, rho ophiuchi, star-forming region, infrared image, wise, emission nebula, reflection nebula
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA

items.title: Jabbah and Associates
items.description_narrative: Wisps of green dust drift across a star-flecked field in this infrared view of Jabbah, whose name means "the forehead of the scorpion." Jabbah lies 440 light-years away and, though it looks like a single star, is actually a whole system of stars lighting the surrounding gas and dust.
items.tags: jabbah, scorpius, infrared imaging, wise, nebula, dust cloud, star system
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA

items.title: Perseus Molecular Cloud
items.description_narrative: The Perseus Molecular Cloud, a collection of gas and dust about 1,000 light-years from Earth and roughly 500 light-years across, hosts an abundance of young stars in this Spitzer infrared view. Fiery orange and red filaments billow through the frame, with bright clustered points marking clumps of newborn stars.
items.tags: molecular cloud, spitzer, infrared, star formation, nebula, gas and dust
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech

items.title: Orion Big Head Revealed in Infrared
items.description_narrative: The Lambda Orionis molecular ring, also called the Meissa Ring, glows across roughly 130 light-years of space in this infrared view from WISE. Wispy green filaments of dust encircle a dark center, with scattered blue stars and small red-orange knots marking pockets of warmer gas.
items.tags: nebula, infrared, wise, molecular ring, star-forming region, dust
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA

items.title: Stars Gather in Downtown Milky Way
items.description_narrative: A hazy blue-green field of stars and dust brightens toward the center, where pink and orange clouds glow amid a dense white core. This infrared view from NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope shows the crowded center of the Milky Way, whose central star cluster lies 26,000 light-years away and spans roughly 2,400 by 1,360 light-years.
items.tags: milky way, galactic center, infrared image, spitzer, star cluster, nebula, dust
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech

items.title: Saturn … Four Years On
items.description_narrative: Cassini assembled this natural-color mosaic from 30 images taken on July 23, 2008, as the spacecraft panned across Saturn and its rings. Pale gold and cream bands wrap the planet's cloud tops, crossed by a wide, thin ring seen nearly edge-on.
items.tags: saturn, rings, cassini, natural color, gas giant, cloud bands
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute

items.title: High Resolution Ceres View
items.description_narrative: Dawn's high-resolution view of Ceres shows a heavily cratered gray sphere, its surface pocked with craters of every size down to fine texture. Near the center, a small cluster of bright white spots marks Occator Crater, the brightest area on the dwarf planet. The image resolves surface features down to about 120 feet per pixel.
items.tags: ceres, dwarf planet, dawn mission, craters, occator crater, planetary science
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA/MPS/DLR/IDA

items.title: On the Final Frontier
items.description_narrative: This natural-color Cassini mosaic, combining 45 images taken over about two hours, looks across Saturn's rings from their unlit side, roughly 1.1 million kilometers from the planet. The planet's banded, pale gold disk glows behind broad dark rings, its own shadow cutting a curved dark bite across the cloud tops.
items.tags: saturn, rings, cassini, planet, natural color, gas giant
items.credit_line: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute

items.title: Webb visits a star-forming spiral
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: Webb's infrared image of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 2283, about 45 million light-years away in Canis Major, combines near- and mid-infrared data. Loose arms of red and orange dust and glowing knots swirl around a pale centre, and a few bright stars carry long spikes.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, infrared, webb, barred spiral, dust, star formation
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Leroy

items.title: Dwarf stars in a glittering sky
items.agent_name: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, V. Almendros-Abad, M. Guarcello, K. Monsch, and the EWOCS team.
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: This Webb infrared image shows the star cluster Westerlund 2 in the stellar nursery Gum 29, about 20,000 light-years away in Carina. Thousands of bright stars with spiked halos crowd a blue haze, framed by ragged orange clouds.
items.tags: star cluster, infrared, webb, nebula, stellar nursery, carina
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, V. Almendros-Abad, M. Guarcello, K. Monsch, and the EWOCS team.

items.title: NGC 602 (Webb image)
items.agent_name: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, P. Zeidler, E. Sabbi, A. Nota, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb)
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: Webb's infrared image shows the young star cluster NGC 602 near the edge of the Small Magellanic Cloud, a satellite galaxy about 200 000 light-years away. A pink glow fills the centre around a small cluster of stars, ringed by ragged orange and teal walls of dust, with distant galaxies scattered behind.
items.tags: star cluster, infrared, webb, nebula, dust, small magellanic cloud
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, P. Zeidler, E. Sabbi, A. Nota, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb)

items.title: Webb opens a Treasure Chest filled with stars
items.agent_name: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, M. Reiter; Acknowledgement: M. H. Özsaraç
items.description_narrative: Webb's NIRCam shows the Treasure Chest, a dust cloud in the Carina Nebula about 7500 light-years away, shaped by radiation and winds from nearby massive stars. Golden folds of dust rise like a tall sculpted form with a bright glow at its crown, set against a teal and red backdrop dense with blue stars.
items.tags: nebula, infrared, webb, dust clouds, carina nebula, star cluster
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, M. Reiter; Acknowledgement: M. H. Özsaraç

items.title: The Red Spider Nebula, caught by Webb
items.agent_name: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, J. H. Kastner (Rochester Institute of Technology)
items.description_narrative: Webb's NIRCam shows NGC 6537, the Red Spider Nebula, a planetary nebula formed from the shed outer layers of a dying star; the central star appears red here because a shroud of hot dust surrounds it. A bright core sits at the waist of an hourglass shape, with an orange-red band across the middle and blue lobes sweeping out to either side through a field packed with stars.
items.tags: planetary nebula, infrared, webb, hourglass, dust, stars
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, J. H. Kastner (Rochester Institute of Technology)

items.title: HH 211 (NIRCam image, cropped)
items.agent_name: ESA/Webb, NASA, CSA, T. Ray (Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies)
items.description_narrative: This Webb image shows Herbig-Haro 211 (HH 211), a bipolar jet from a very young protostar about 1,000 light-years away in Perseus. A narrow jet runs diagonally across a dark blue field, ending in glowing pink bow-shaped shock fronts on either side.
items.tags: protostar, jet, infrared, webb, herbig-haro, outflow
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA, CSA, T. Ray (Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies)

items.title: Messier 77 (MIRI + NIRCam)
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: Webb's image of Messier 77, a barred spiral galaxy about 45 million light-years away in Cetus, has a bright active nucleus at its heart. The orange lines radiating from the centre are diffraction spikes from the telescope's optics, not structure in the galaxy itself. Rust-red spiral arms wind around a pale glowing core.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, infrared, webb, active nucleus, dust, starburst
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Leroy

items.title: Fireworks of stellar starbursts
items.agent_name: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Adamo (Stockholm University) and the FEAST JWST team
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: This Webb infrared image shows NGC 4449, a dwarf starburst galaxy about 12.5 million light-years away in Canes Venatici. The orange-red areas trace carbon-based molecules called PAHs, while hydrogen ionised by newly formed stars appears as bright red spots. Fine blue stars glow across the centre.
items.tags: dwarf galaxy, starburst, infrared, webb, star formation, hydrogen
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Adamo (Stockholm University) and the FEAST JWST team

items.title: A galactic treasury
items.agent_name: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Leroy, J. Lee and the PHANGS Team
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: Webb's view of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 1559, about 35 million light-years away in Reticulum, pairs the dust glow seen by MIRI with starlight from NIRCam. A pale blue bar of starlight crosses the centre, surrounded by orange and pink arms with bright clumps.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, barred spiral, infrared, webb, dust, reticulum
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Leroy, J. Lee and the PHANGS Team

items.title: Tracing spiral arms in infrared
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: Webb's image of the spiral galaxy NGC 2090 in Columba combines NIRCam and MIRI data, with starlight shown in blue and dust emission in red. A tilted galaxy with a glowing cyan core is encircled by two winding arms of red and orange dust.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, infrared, webb, dust, spiral arms, columba
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Leroy

items.title: Close look at a local galaxy
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: This Webb image shows the spiral galaxy NGC 2566 in Puppis, about 76 million light-years away, with a long central bar and well-defined arms. Rings of red and orange dust surround a blue-white glowing centre, with dark gaps between the arms.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, barred spiral, infrared, webb, dust, puppis
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Leroy

items.title: The stellar lifecycle in a nearby spiral
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: Webb's MIRI and NIRCam together image the spiral galaxy NGC 5134, about 65 million light-years away in Virgo, where gas clouds along the arms are sites of star formation. A tilted ellipse of red arms glows inside a soft bluish halo around a bright centre.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, infrared, webb, star formation, gas clouds, virgo
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Leroy

items.title: Peeking into Perseus
items.agent_name: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Scholz, K. Muzic, A. Langeveld, R. Jayawardhana
items.description_narrative: This Webb mosaic shows NGC 1333, a young star-forming cluster in the Perseus molecular cloud about 960 light-years away, seen through infrared light that pierces its dust. Some of the faintest points are newborn brown dwarfs, and the Herbig-Haro objects mark active star formation. Pale blue and copper clouds drift around a dark rising column of dust, with a few bright spiked stars scattered across the scene.
items.tags: nebula, infrared, webb, star-forming region, brown dwarfs, perseus molecular cloud
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Scholz, K. Muzic, A. Langeveld, R. Jayawardhana

items.title: NGC 3256 (HST)
items.description_narrative: Hubble's image shows NGC 3256, a galaxy distorted by an ancient head-on merger of two spirals, likely about 500 million years ago. Dark brown dust lanes spiral through a bright white core inside a wide, smoky halo.
items.tags: galaxy merger, hubble, dust lanes, spiral galaxy, star formation, interacting galaxies
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble, NASA

items.title: IRS 3 Field (NIRCam and MIRI image)
items.agent_name: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, F. Peißker, J. Lu, F. Yusef-Zadeh, N. B. Sabha, C. Chan
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: Webb's mid-infrared view covers the field around the evolved star IRS 3, which lies 0.55 light-years from Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the Milky Way's centre. The team found that IRS 3 keeps producing fresh material close to the black hole, even in that harsh radiation. A dense field of blue and white stars is swathed in red and orange glowing clouds, brightest at the centre.
items.tags: galactic centre, infrared, webb, dust, star field, black hole
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, F. Peißker, J. Lu, F. Yusef-Zadeh, N. B. Sabha, C. Chan

items.title: Westerlund 1 (wide-field view)
items.agent_name: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb), M. G. Guarcello (INAF-OAPA) and the EWOCS team
items.description_narrative: Webb's NIRCam shows the open cluster Westerlund 1, about 12 000 light-years away in Ara, a super star cluster discovered in 1961. Bright stars with long crossed spikes dominate a dense field, with a few red wisps of gas near the middle.
items.tags: star cluster, super star cluster, infrared, webb, massive stars, ara
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb), M. G. Guarcello (INAF-OAPA) and the EWOCS team

items.title: Clash of the Titans
items.agent_name: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, L. Armus, A. Evans
items.medium: Infrared image — Webb NIRCam and MIRI
items.description_narrative: Webb's infrared image of NGC 3256, about 120 million light-years away in Vela, shows the aftermath of a collision between two spiral galaxies that astronomers date to around 500 million years ago. The collision set off a burst of star formation. A bright orange and white spiral core sits inside a wide grey halo, with red streams curving away to one side.
items.tags: galaxy merger, infrared, webb, star formation, interacting galaxies, vela
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, L. Armus, A. Evans

items.title: Striking star clusters and irregular clumps
items.description_narrative: Webb's infrared image shows Arp 263, also catalogued as NGC 3239, an irregular galaxy about 25 million light-years away in Leo. Red patches of glowing gas are scattered through a pale haze of stars. The bright spiked star at the top is BD+17 2217, a star in our own galaxy.
items.tags: irregular galaxy, infrared, webb, star formation, galaxy merger, leo
items.credit_line: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Leroy

items.title: Tangled — cosmic edition
items.description_narrative: Hubble's image shows SNR 0454-67.2, a supernova remnant in the Large Magellanic Cloud, likely left by a Type Ia explosion. Thin red threads loop and snake through dark clouds against a dense field of blue and orange stars.
items.tags: supernova remnant, hubble, large magellanic cloud, gas filaments, stars, type ia supernova
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble, NASA

items.title: The young stars of Taurus
items.description_narrative: Hubble's image shows the reflection nebula GN 04.32.8, part of the Taurus Molecular Cloud about 480 light-years away, lit by the triple star system HP Tau, HP Tau G2 and HP Tau G3. Pale blue-grey clouds curl around a few bright spiked stars, with dark voids in the nebula.
items.tags: reflection nebula, hubble, taurus, dust, young stars, stellar nursery
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, G. Duchêne

items.title: Capturing candyfloss clouds
items.description_narrative: Wispy clouds in teal, pink and rust drift across a dense scatter of tiny stars, with one orange star trailing long spikes. This is the Large Magellanic Cloud, a dwarf galaxy beside the Milky Way, imaged by Hubble with the Wide Field Camera 3 through several filters that include ultraviolet and infrared light.
items.tags: nebula, dwarf galaxy, hubble, gas clouds, stars, large magellanic cloud
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, C. Murray

items.title: A glittering cluster shines again
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA, A. Sarajedini, G. Piotto, M. Libralato
items.description_narrative: A round swarm of stars thickens toward the middle, where the points glow blue-white, while orange stars stand out around the edges. This is the globular cluster Messier 72 in Aquarius, revisited by Hubble with ultraviolet data added; the colours separate hot blue stars from cooler red giants.
items.tags: globular cluster, star cluster, hubble, messier 72, stars, aquarius
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, A. Sarajedini, G. Piotto, M. Libralato

items.title: Extreme star cluster bursts into life in new Hubble image
items.agent_name: NASA, ESA and the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration
items.description_narrative: A tight knot of bright blue-white stars sits in the middle, with rust-coloured ridges of gas curling around it on the right. The star-forming region NGC 3603, seen by Hubble, holds a massive young cluster whose hot blue stars have cleared a large cavity in the surrounding gas.
items.tags: star cluster, nebula, ngc 3603, hubble, star formation, gas and dust
items.credit_line: NASA, ESA and the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration

items.title: Festive and Free-Floating
items.description_narrative: A sea of red glow fills the frame, dotted with sharp stars, and dark teardrop-shaped silhouettes hang in it with a larger dark mass rising at the lower right. Hubble photographed a small part of the nebula Westerhout 5, where the dark tadpole shape at upper left is a free-floating evaporating gaseous globule; the red comes from hydrogen emission.
items.tags: nebula, red glow, dark globule, hubble, westerhout 5, stars
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, R. Sahai

items.title: Tempestuous Young Stars in Orion
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA, J. Bally, M. Robberto
items.description_narrative: Two bright stars with cross-shaped spikes sit in drifting haze that is red at the left and a glowing blue at the lower right. The brighter star is the variable V 372 Orionis in the Orion Nebula, imaged by Hubble using two instruments; the four spikes are diffraction from the telescope's own structure.
items.tags: orion nebula, variable star, hubble, diffraction spikes, nebula, young stars
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, J. Bally, M. Robberto

items.title: Into the storm
items.description_narrative: Blue-white veils of gas and dark brown dust lanes swirl through a field crowded with stars, with a brighter pale blue cloud at the lower right. Hubble shows N159, a star-forming region in the Large Magellanic Cloud, where the glow of hydrogen and strong stellar winds shape the surrounding material around the Papillon Nebula.
items.tags: nebula, star-forming region, n159, large magellanic cloud, hubble, dust lanes
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA

items.title: A Scattering of Stars
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA, J. Kalirai, A. Milone
items.description_narrative: Hundreds of blue stars spread out from a dense, bright core against black space, with a few orange stars among them and a faint red haze in the upper corner. This is the open cluster NGC 330 in the Small Magellanic Cloud, seen by Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3; the crossed spikes around stars come from the telescope's supporting vanes.
items.tags: open cluster, star cluster, ngc 330, hubble, small magellanic cloud, stars
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, J. Kalirai, A. Milone

items.title: Hubble Inspects A Pair of Space Oddities
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA, Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA, J. Dalcanton
items.description_narrative: Two spiral galaxies sit at opposite ends of a pale blue stream of stars that arcs between them, with a small tilted galaxy in the gap. Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys captured two members of the galaxy triplet Arp 248, also called Wild's Triplet, in Virgo, joined by a tidal tail from their mutual gravity.
items.tags: galaxies, interacting galaxies, tidal tail, arp 248, hubble, virgo
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA, J. Dalcanton

items.title: Long-distance relationship
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA, J. Dalcanton, Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA
items.description_narrative: A small bright spiral with tightly wound arms sits at the left, beside a much larger, dim galaxy with a loose ring of blue knots. Hubble pictures Arp 4 in Cetus, from the Atlas of Peculiar Galaxies; the two are not neighbours, since the large one, MCG-02-05-050, lies far closer to us than its companion.
items.tags: galaxies, spiral galaxy, arp 4, hubble, cetus, low surface brightness
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, J. Dalcanton, Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA

items.title: A glimpse of the future
items.description_narrative: A bright, tangled core sits in the middle with two long, thin curving streams of blue stars sweeping out to opposite sides. Hubble shows NGC 2623, also called Arp 243, in Cancer, the result of a collision between two galaxies; its tidal tails and blue clusters mark the burst of star formation.
items.tags: merging galaxies, ngc 2623, tidal tails, hubble, arp 243, star formation
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA

items.title: Hubble Gazes into M74
items.description_narrative: A face-on spiral shows a pale glowing centre, dark winding dust threads, and many pink and red patches strung along blue-grey arms. This is M74, the Phantom Galaxy, in Pisces, imaged by Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys; the pink blooms are hydrogen clouds lit by hot young stars.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, m74, phantom galaxy, hubble, h ii regions, pisces
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, R. Chandar

items.title: Grand swirls
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA; Acknowledgement: Flickr user Det58
items.description_narrative: A bright, small centre is wrapped in broad sweeping arms edged with dark dust and pale pink star clusters, against a dark blue background. This is NGC 1566, a Seyfert galaxy in Dorado, taken by Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 in near-infrared light.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, ngc 1566, seyfert galaxy, hubble, dorado, near-infrared
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA; Acknowledgement: Flickr user Det58

items.title: A galactic maelstrom
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA and the LEGUS Team; Acknowledgement: R. Gendler
items.description_narrative: A large glowing core is off-centre inside faint arms, with dark dust lanes spiralling inward and blue-white clusters along the outer edge. Hubble shows Messier 96, a lopsided spiral in Leo that is similar to the Milky Way in mass and size, with gravity from nearby group members thought to have disturbed its arms.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, messier 96, asymmetric galaxy, hubble, leo, dust lanes
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA and the LEGUS Team; Acknowledgement: R. Gendler

items.title: Birds of a Feather
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA, J. Lee and the PHANGS-HST Team; Acknowledgement: Judy Schmidt (Geckzilla)
items.description_narrative: A smooth, pale yellow oval core is ringed by short, ragged arms of dark dust threaded with small blue stars, like layered feathers. Hubble pictures NGC 2775, a flocculent spiral in Cancer, whose feathery arms show quiet recent star formation and whose large central bulge has little gas left.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, flocculent spiral, ngc 2775, hubble, cancer, dust lanes
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, J. Lee and the PHANGS-HST Team; Acknowledgement: Judy Schmidt (Geckzilla)

items.title: The squid and the whale
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA, L. C. Ho, D. Thilker
items.description_narrative: A bright whitish core is wrapped in swirling pink-flecked arms and dark red dust, with one bright star with sharp spikes at the lower left. This is Messier 77, nicknamed the Squid Galaxy, in Cetus, imaged by Hubble; its filaments curl around the disc like tentacles, and this version adds newer filters and processing.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, messier 77, squid galaxy, hubble, cetus, dust lanes
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, L. C. Ho, D. Thilker

items.title: Starbursts on grand scale
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA, F. Belfiore, J. Lee and the PHANGS-HST Team
items.description_narrative: Two broad spiral arms sweep around a bright centre, glittering with blue clusters and scattered pink and red patches. Hubble photographed NGC 5248, also known as Caldwell 45, a grand design spiral in Boötes with many starburst regions and a nuclear ring around its core.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, ngc 5248, caldwell 45, hubble, starburst, boötes
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, F. Belfiore, J. Lee and the PHANGS-HST Team

items.title: Finding star clusters in the Lost Galaxy
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA, F. Belfiore, J. Lee and the PHANGS-HST Team
items.description_narrative: Broad spiral arms wind around a glowing core, strung with blue star clusters and pink glowing patches, with a few bright spiked stars in front. Hubble shows NGC 4535, the Lost Galaxy, in Virgo, where young star clusters sit inside glowing H II regions that mark especially hot, massive stars.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, ngc 4535, lost galaxy, hubble, virgo, h ii regions
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, F. Belfiore, J. Lee and the PHANGS-HST Team

items.title: Snapshot of a peculiar spiral
items.agent_name: ESA/Hubble & NASA, J. Dalcanton, R. J. Foley (UC Santa Cruz), C. Kilpatrick
items.description_narrative: One thick, star-speckled arm sweeps up toward the viewer, wrapped around a bright, warm core, while the far side is faint and wispy. Hubble captured Arp 184, also catalogued as NGC 1961, in Camelopardalis, a skewed spiral that earned its place in Halton Arp's Atlas of Peculiar Galaxies for that single broad arm.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, arp 184, ngc 1961, hubble, camelopardalis, peculiar galaxy
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA, J. Dalcanton, R. J. Foley (UC Santa Cruz), C. Kilpatrick

items.title: Edge-on beauty
items.description_narrative: A thin, tilted band of pale light crosses the frame diagonally, split by a ragged lane of brown dust and blue stars, with a few bright stars and tiny galaxies around it. Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys imaged the northern half of NGC 891 in Andromeda, a spiral seen exactly edge-on, where filaments of dust and gas rise out of the disc.
items.tags: spiral galaxy, edge-on galaxy, ngc 891, hubble, andromeda, dust lanes
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA; Acknowledgement: Nick Rose

items.title: A wanderer dancing the dance of stars and space
items.description_narrative: A bright, tight whirl of blue-white stars circles a glowing yellow centre, inside a broad, hazy oval of arms that run off the edges of the frame. This is the star-forming ring around the heart of NGC 1097, a barred Seyfert galaxy in Fornax, taken by Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys with visual and infrared filters.
items.tags: barred spiral, ngc 1097, seyfert galaxy, hubble, fornax, star-forming ring
items.credit_line: ESA/Hubble & NASA; Acknowledgement: E. Sturdivant
